_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); gold-miner signals with Newmont's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Newmont is the world’s leading gold company and is the only gold company included in the S&P 500 Index and Fortune 500.' 'Our business is dependent on the prices of gold, silver, copper, zinc and lead, which fluctuate on a daily basis and are affected by numerous factors beyond our control.' 'A substantial or extended decline in gold, silver, copper, zinc or lead prices would have a material adverse effect on us.' 'The metals markets are cyclical' (the FY2019 10-K's own words; it calls the metals markets it sells into cyclical, so CYCLICAL, the CB rule); no disruption theme in the registry is live for a gold miner on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing', ECOMMERCE to 'e-commerce (Amazon effect) displaces physical retail, malls, grocery, distribution', STREAMING to 'cord-cutting / streaming displaces linear TV networks and pay-TV bundles', ENERGY_TRANSITION to 'decarbonisation strands oil, gas and coal reserves and refining', EV to 'battery-electric vehicles displace ICE powertrains, auto parts suppliers and fuel retail', CRYPTO to 'crypto / DeFi disintermediates payments networks, banks, exchanges, remittance': none names a miner), so the watch list is empty; Newmont holds no oil, gas or coal reserves and no refining, so ENERGY_TRANSITION is read as out of scope, and the 10-K's own climate words are a cost, not a stranded reserve: 'Legislation and increased regulation and requirements regarding climate change are resulting in increased costs on us, our venture partners and our suppliers, including increased energy, capital equipment, environmental monitoring and reporting and other costs to comply with such regulations.' (the FY2019 10-K's risk factor) (text only)

BEAR.desc: Flat EPS (no EPS change in FY10-FY14 ex-FY11 ex-FY13 to measure: the 0% cap); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +12.6%/yr (Q3 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 9.0-yr ex-FY11 ex-FY13 ex-FY15 ex-FY16 ex-FY17 ex-FY18 ex-FY19 median

BULL.desc: EPS +12.6%/yr (FY10-FY14 ex-FY11 ex-FY13 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +12.6%/yr (best 2-yr run FY10-FY14 ex-FY11 ex-FY13, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NEM (retrospective, 2021-01-08) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 13.41x (74.1% downside to Bear $16.26 / +5.5% upside to Bull $66.26) | Adj composite 1.95 vs market 3.77: gap -1.82 [OVERVALUED] | +123% above the EPP floor $28.16 (22x FY20E $1.28) | Conservative 2-yr case: -49.9% total (-24.9%/yr) | At 49.1x FY20E the 15% hurdle price $83.04 sits above the BULL case; revenue +16.8% YoY in Q3 2020, forward revenues +16.8% (Q3 2020 revenue growth (no revenue guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
